the development of a new method to resolve the SIRE or SAS phase ambiguity, which has been successfully applied to a number of protein structures at resolutions as low as 3 A.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new scheme is to be preferred for the resolution range 4-2.5 A, and the older method for lower resolution.
the CC-based method is a very good one, and that the complex-based method is a better one.
the CC-based method is the best of the available procedures for resolving the SIS phase ambiguity at low resolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of the two criteria, the CC and the average phase, provides an effective and efficient procedure for the resolution of the SIR or SAR phase ambiguity.
the new method has a 100% success rate in resolving the SIR and SAS phases at 2.5 A resolution, whereas the old method has a 90% success rate.
the new method can resolve the phase ambiguity for all cases where the CC is greater than 0.5, whereas the old method can do so only if the CC is greater 0.8.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to validate the quality of a map, and the CC between /F(h)/ values and /X(h)/ values is an important measure to use in that regard.
the SIR or Sas phase ambiguity can be resolved with high reliability by using a single map.
the CC is a useful criterion in map validation and refinement, but the complex correlation coefficient (CCC) is more powerful.
